summary: Today’s PaymentsDive recap: 8 new stories, with focus on fraud/security, regulation.

articles.title: Visa builds business abroad
articles.description: The card network has entered a partnership with an international lender in emerging economies to fuel demand for digital payments around the world.

articles.title: Block seeks OCC bank charter
articles.description: Cash App’s parent is joining a parade of fintechs seeking to become national banks as the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency allows more leeway for such licenses.

articles.title: Processor pays $12M to settle ‘sham’ merchant case
articles.description: ISO Humboldt Merchant Services agreed to settle a Federal Trade Commission lawsuit that alleged it processed fraudulent payments.

articles.title: RTP, Fed race on fast payments
articles.description: While The Clearing House’s RTP network races with the Federal Reserve’s FedNow system, the U.S., overall, lags on speedy payments.

articles.title: Nuvei pays $4.9M to settle FTC case
articles.description: The company has agreed to settle a Federal Trade Commission lawsuit that alleged it handled processing for merchants that were engaged in scams.

articles.title: Subscription spending climbs
articles.description: Consumers are splurging more via subscription payments, often for fashion and entertainment, a new Bank of America report says.

articles.title: Ramp takes on AI expense
articles.description: The expense-management company has expanded into the nascent field of artificial intelligence routing as companies seek to keep tabs on their AI costs.

articles.title: Fiserv explores divestitures
articles.description: The payments processor, under pressure amid management upheaval and client attrition, told analysts it’s still considering the sale of a debit network.
